# Forensic Dossier — Nemetschek SE (NEM.DE)

*A deep dive on management and the setup. Prepared for the investment committee. All figures in euros unless noted; the company reports in euros, and some product prices are quoted in US dollars.*

**One-line frame:** Nemetschek is a high-quality German building-and-design software compounder in the middle of a successful shift to subscriptions — but it is priced like one of the most expensive software names in its industry, not like a bargain. The screener flagged it as "deep value" on a stale price and a broken fair-value estimate; the forensic read says the opposite. This is a great business at a demanding price, not a cheap stock.

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Across the eight-ish quarters of calls we have (mid-2024 through late-2025), the story is remarkably consistent and, unusually, it has been *delivered* rather than merely promised.

- **The spine of the story is the subscription transition.** Management's stated "clear number one priority" is moving the whole portfolio from perpetual licenses (a one-time sale) and maintenance contracts to subscription and software-as-a-service (software rented annually, recognized over time). In H1 2024 recurring revenue was ~85% of the total; by full-year 2024 it was 86.5%; by Q1 2026 it hit a record **95%**. That is the single most important number in the whole file, and it went the way management said it would, quarter after quarter.

- **Growth drivers introduced and kept:** (1) Bluebeam — the US-standard collaboration tool for construction — completing its subscription conversion and being pushed internationally; (2) the July 2024 GoCanvas acquisition (field-worker data collection), the largest deal in company history at the time, to reach construction's field workers; (3) a steadily louder artificial-intelligence pitch (the "AI and Data Innovation Hub," agentic assistants, the Firmus AI bolt-on, and by late 2025 "Bluebeam Max," an AI add-on package); (4) internationalization, especially India and Saudi Arabia.

- **What quietly changed:** the AI narrative went from a paragraph in 2024 to the *centerpiece* of the Q3 2025 call ("what is currently one of, if not the most important topic for us"). That is a tell worth watching — it is both a genuine product effort and a fashionable thing to emphasize while the multiple is high. Separately, two large deals bookend the file: GoCanvas in 2024 and, most importantly, the **$2.4B HCSS acquisition announced April 2026 and closed July 1, 2026** — heavy-civil contractor software (HeavyBid, HeavyJob) bought from private-equity firm Thoma Bravo, at roughly 20 times HCSS's expected 2025 earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA). That deal is not in the transcripts but is the most consequential recent event and reshapes the balance sheet.

The arc, in short: a disciplined, on-plan transition story that has broadened from "convert to subscription" to "convert, then bolt on adjacent construction software and layer AI on top."

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

The financials corroborate management's claims closely — this is a high-credibility file. Where the tension lies is not in the operating results but in valuation.

| Management claim | The hard numbers | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "High, profitable growth" | Revenue €681M (2021) → €802M → €852M → €996M → **€1.19B (2025)**, a ~15% five-year compound annual growth rate; net income €135M → €217M | **Matches.** Steady, real, accelerating growth. |
| Subscription share rising | Recurring revenue 85% (H1'24) → 86.5% (FY'24) → **95% (Q1'26)** | **Matches, and then some.** |
| Margin expansion despite transition drag | Gross margin 49.4% and expanding; EBITDA margin reached 32.5% in Q3'25; FY'26 guide 32–33% | **Matches.** Operating leverage is real. |
| Strong cash generation | Free cash flow margin ~31%; trailing-twelve-month free cash flow €377M; free cash flow compounding ~24%/yr over three years | **Matches.** Cash conversion above 1.0, as the CFO promised, driven by prepaid subscriptions. |
| Guidance delivery | Beat 5 of 7 recent quarters (~71%); 2024 organic growth came in at +14% vs a 10–11% guide | **Matches — mild sandbagging.** They set beatable bars. |
| Returns on capital | Return on equity ~23%, return on invested capital ~16% | **Solid, not spectacular.** Good but not a fortress-level return, and note return on invested capital (~16%) is only modestly above the cost of capital. |

**Where the story is richer than the trajectory justifies — valuation, not operations.** The screener's headline — "Fair Value €114, Margin of Safety 122%" — is an artifact of a Buffett/Graham-style model that does not fit a 45-times-cash-flow software name. The screener's *own* honest signals sit right next to it and point the other way: DCF (discounted cash flow) fair value **€46** (a discount that is actually a *premium* — the stock is above it), and earnings-power value **−100%** (i.e., current earnings power supports roughly half the price or less). Live market data confirm the honest read: Nemetschek trades around **49x EV/EBITDA and ~78x trailing earnings**, versus Autodesk near **25x EV/EBITDA and ~19x forward earnings**. Nemetschek is not cheaper than its US peers — it is roughly **twice as expensive** on cash-flow multiples. The "122% margin of safety" is false.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rising and steady — one of the more confident management teams in the file.**

- H1 2024: "exactly where we wanted to be after the first six months" — calm, on-plan.
- Q3 2024: navigated a deliberately tough comparison in Design ("very high comparison base") without flinching; Build growth *accelerated* to +15%.
- FY 2024 (Mar 2025): "achieved or even clearly exceeded every single one of our financial goals in 2024."
- Q3 2025: "another very successful quarter," EBITDA margin 32.5%, earnings per share +40.7%.

The language stays offensive (growth, investment, AI, internationalization) rather than defensive (cost, macro survival). Notably, when analysts pressed on soft construction macro, the CEO reframed it as a *tailwind* for digitization ("business as usual is not an option") rather than retreating. Confidence is earned by the delivery record, not bluster. The one honest wobble: a "low-teens million euro" one-off hit in H1 2025 from "the unexpected insolvency of a service and payment provider" — disclosed plainly, not buried.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**High.** The clearest evidence: 2024 organic, currency-adjusted growth landed at +14% against an initial 10–11% guide — a clean beat, not a lowered-then-hit maneuver. The ~71% beat rate over seven quarters corroborates a pattern of setting achievable targets and clearing them. For 2026 they guide 14–15% organic growth and a 32–33% EBITDA margin, and Q1 2026 already printed +17% currency-adjusted revenue growth with guidance reaffirmed. There is a mild sandbagging habit — they guide conservatively and beat — which is the *good* kind of credibility problem. **Reliability: High.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Design-segment normalized growth.** Analysts (Goldman's Agarwal, ODDO's David) repeatedly probed what Design grows at *after* the subscription transition ends and the temporary multi-year-contract tailwind fades. Management conceded it settles to "high single digits… ending up mid-single digits." This is the honest soft spot: a chunk of current Design momentum is transition mechanics (pulling maintenance customers onto multi-year subscriptions early), not durable underlying demand.
- **Macro resilience vs. peers.** Analysts kept asking why Nemetschek isn't seeing the construction slowdown its peers cite. Management's answer (digitization-as-necessity) is plausible but is the kind of claim that only gets tested in a real downturn.
- **Bluebeam Max pricing and mix.** UBS's Briest pushed on where Bluebeam Max would be priced and whether users move up the tiers. Management deferred pricing to Q1 2026 — since answered: Bluebeam Max launched globally in May 2026 at an introductory **$590 per user per year**, above the $440 "Complete" tier. Monetization of AI is real but early.

No obvious pattern of deflection that later turned into bad news — the deflections were about *future* normalized growth rates, which is legitimate uncertainty rather than evasion.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🟢 Recurring revenue at 95% (Q1'26) — the transition is essentially done, which de-risks future revenue.
🟢 Guidance beaten repeatedly; management says what it will do and does it.
🟢 Free cash flow margin ~31% with cash conversion above 1.0 — genuinely high-quality earnings.
🟢 Build segment (Bluebeam + GoCanvas) accelerating; strong US demand held up through soft macro.

🔴 **Valuation is the whole risk.** At ~49x EV/EBITDA and ~78x earnings, the price already discounts years of flawless execution. Any stumble re-rates hard.
🔴 **Design's post-transition growth settles to mid-single digits** on management's own words — a meaningful deceleration once the multi-year-contract sugar-high rolls off.
🔴 **Balance sheet is levering up for HCSS.** The deal adds ~€450M of net debt and brings Thoma Bravo in as a ~28% minority owner of the enlarged Build & Construct segment — a structural complication and integration risk on top of the still-digesting GoCanvas deal. Net debt was already recomputed to ~€53M as of Q1 2026; the HCSS refinancing takes it materially higher.
🔴 **AI is being emphasized precisely while the multiple is stretched** — the narrative is doing some of the work the fundamentals can't do at this price.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- **The AI pivot in emphasis.** Between 2024 and late 2025, AI moved from a supporting line to the headline. Genuine (Firmus AI acquisition, agentic assistants, Google Cloud/Stanford/NTU partnerships), but the *volume* of AI talk rises as the valuation gets harder to defend on cash flow alone.
- **Deal cadence is accelerating.** GoCanvas (2024) → Firmus AI + Manufacton (2025) → HCSS at $2.4B (2026). Management repeatedly calls M&A "a cornerstone of our strategy." This is a serial acquirer funding growth partly through deals — which works beautifully in a bull market and strains when financing tightens.
- **Thoma Bravo rolling into the Build segment** rather than taking all cash is an interesting structural signal — a sophisticated software private-equity seller keeping a stake suggests they see more upside, but it also creates a future liquidity/governance question at the segment level.
- **CFO's cash-conversion framing** ("prepayment models… you should expect that above one in the future as long as we are growing") is a subtle but important tell: the cash-flow quality is *structurally* tied to continued growth. If growth stalls, the deferred-revenue tailwind reverses.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Classification: STRENGTHENING** (operations) / **but priced for perfection** (valuation).

The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: **this is a genuinely excellent, well-managed compounding business trading at roughly twice its US peers' cash-flow multiple and well above the screener's own honest fair value (~€46 discounted cash flow vs. ~€61–63 market).** The "deep value / 122% margin of safety" label that brought this name to committee is wrong — it comes from a stale ~€55 scan price and a Buffett-style €114 fair value that does not apply to a 45x-cash-flow software stock. There is no discrete, dated catalyst here; the only "event" is the HCSS close (July 1, 2026), which *adds* leverage and integration risk rather than unlocking hidden value. The right question is not "how much upside from a re-rate" but "is the quality worth paying a full-to-rich price for" — and at ~49x EV/EBITDA, the answer for a value-discipline book is no.

**Economic moat: NARROW-to-WIDE, and durable.** The moat is genuine **switching-cost plus intangible-brand**: architecture, engineering and construction professionals build their workflows and file formats around Allplan, Vectorworks, Graphisoft and Bluebeam, and Bluebeam is the de-facto US standard for construction markup. Returns support it — return on equity ~23%, return on invested capital ~16%, gross margin ~49% and *expanding*, EBITDA margin rising to 32%+. That is a **widening**, not eroding, franchise. Call it a solid narrow-to-wide moat that is getting wider as the subscription base compounds.

**Secular threat: MANAGEABLE.** Generative AI is the one structural question for any design-software incumbent — the risk that AI tools collapse the value of "good-enough" design output. But Nemetschek's moat is hard workflow and file-format lock-in in a regulated, liability-heavy industry (buildings that must not fall down), not a thin creative-tooling habit. So far AI is landing as an *upsell* (Bluebeam Max at $590/user) rather than a disruptor, and adoption data management cited (AI used in ~48% of design tasks) points to augmentation. This is not a melting terminal value; it is a manageable, watch-it risk. The cheapness question is moot anyway — the stock is not cheap.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Across the eight-ish quarters of calls we have (mid-2024 through late-2025), the story is remarkably consistent and, unusually, it has been *delivered* rather than merely promised.

- **The spine of the story is the subscription transition.** Management's stated "clear number one priority" is moving the whole portfolio from perpetual licenses (a one-time sale) and maintenance contracts to subscription and software-as-a-service (software rented annually, recognized over time). 🟢 Recurring revenue at 95% (Q1'26) — the transition is essentially done, which de-risks future revenue.
🟢 Guidance beaten repeatedly; management says what it will do and does it.
🟢 Free cash flow margin ~31% with cash conversion above 1.0 — genuinely high-quality earnings.
🟢 Build segment (Bluebeam + GoCanvas) accelerating; strong US demand held up through soft macro.

🔴 **Valuation is the whole risk.** At ~49x EV/EBITDA and ~78x earnings, the price already discounts years of flawless execution. Any stumble re-rates hard.
🔴 **Design's post-transition growth settles to mid-single digits** on management's own words — a meaningful deceleration once the multi-year-contract sugar-high rolls off.
🔴 **Balance sheet is levering up for HCSS.** The deal adds ~€450M of net debt and brings Thoma Bravo in as a ~28% minority owner of the enlarged Build & Construct segment — a structural complication and integration risk on top of the still-digesting GoCanvas deal. 🔴 **AI is being emphasized precisely while the multiple is stretched** — the narrative is doing some of the work the fundamentals can't do at this price.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- **The AI pivot in emphasis.** Between 2024 and late 2025, AI moved from a supporting line to the headline. Genuine (Firmus AI acquisition, agentic assistants, Google Cloud/Stanford/NTU partnerships), but the *volume* of AI talk rises as the valuation gets harder to defend on cash flow alone.
- **Deal cadence is accelerating.** GoCanvas (2024) → Firmus AI + Manufacton (2025) → HCSS at $2.4B (2026). Management repeatedly calls M&A "a cornerstone of our strategy." This is a serial acquirer funding growth partly through deals — which works beautifully in a bull market and strains when financing tightens.
- **Thoma Bravo rolling into the Build segment** rather than taking all cash is an interesting structural signal — a sophisticated software private-equity seller keeping a stake suggests they see more upside, but it also creates a future liquidity/governance question at the segment level.
- **CFO's cash-conversion framing** ("prepayment models… you should expect that above one in the future as long as we are growing") is a subtle but important tell: the cash-flow quality is *structurally* tied to continued growth. If growth stalls, the deferred-revenue tailwind reverses.

**Classification: STRENGTHENING** (operations) / **but priced for perfection** (valuation).
